title: Electricity Markets as a Sabzi Mandi: Market Microstructure Lessons from Indian Power Exchanges

authors.name: Komal Kaur
affiliations: Former Lead Engineer – Power Purchase & ABT (2019–2025), Tata Power Company Ltd – Power System Control Centre, Trombay Thermal Power Station, Mumbai

abstract: This paper examines Indian electricity markets through the analogy of traditional agricultural spot markets — locally known as sabzi mandis — to illuminate fundamental dynamics of price discovery, bidding behavior, volatility, and allocation efficiency in formal power exchanges. While electricity markets operate through sophisticated exchange mechanisms such as the Day-Ahead Market (DAM), Real-Time Market (RTM), and Green Day-Ahead Market (GDAM), many of their underlying behavioral and structural dynamics bear a striking resemblance to informal commodity markets characterized by perishable goods, fluctuating supply, demand shocks, strategic bidding, and time-sensitive clearing decisions. Drawing on market microstructure theory, auction design literature, and practitionerinformed perspectives on Indian power markets, this paper develops a four-proposition analytical framework that maps key behavioral drivers — perishability-induced urgency, information asymmetry, behavioral volatility, and flexibility premia — from the mandi context onto power exchange outcomes. The study argues that informal market analogies, far from being mere rhetorical devices, offer structurally valid insights into improving efficiency, procurement strategy, and market design in emerging power markets.
